title: A Translational Note on AI Safety Evaluation
abstract: arXiv:2609.06573v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Recent studies report that automated red-teaming finds more vulnerabilities, at lower cost, than human red-teaming on standard AI safety benchmarks, and some read this as evidence that human evaluators are becoming dispensable. The comparison measures one thing and the conclusion claims another. A benchmark measures how thoroughly an attacker searches a predefined set of harms, fixed in advance by the developers, and a harm left out of that set is invisible to any attacker working inside it, automated or not. The same blind spot appeared in academic cryptography and in clinical drug trials, where an evaluation that was internally valid stayed silent about the population it was never pointed at. We call the AI-safety version the \emph{threat-model coverage gap}, and find that it persists in a current open-weight model, where harms surface in non-English prompts that English benchmarks miss. translated_title: 关于人工智能安全评估的转化性札记
translated_abstract: 最近的研究报告称，在标准AI安全基准测试中，自动化红队测试比人工红队测试能以更低的成本发现更多漏洞，一些人将此解读为人类评估者正变得可有可无的证据。然而，这一比较衡量的是一件事，而其结论宣称的却是另一件事。基准测试衡量的是攻击者在开发者预先固定的预定义危害集合中搜索的彻底程度，而任何在该集合内部运作的攻击者——无论是否自动化——都无法察觉被排除在该集合之外的危害。同样的盲点曾出现在学术密码学和临床药物试验中：在那儿，内部有效的评估对它从未指向的人群保持沉默。我们将AI安全领域的这种现象称为“威胁模型覆盖缺口”，并发现该缺口在当前的一个开源权重模型中依然存在：危害在非英语提示中显现出来，而英语基准测试未能捕捉到它们。要弥合这一缺口，需要评估者的部署方式……（原文摘要不完整）
tldr: 论文提出“威胁模型覆盖缺口”概念，指出自动化红队优于人工红队的结论只是基于预先定义的危害集合内的比较，基准之外的危害（如非英语提示中的风险）对所有评估者都不可见，因此人类评估者并未过时、仍然不可或缺。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces the "threat-model coverage gap," showing that automated red-teaming's apparent superiority over humans only holds within predefined benchmark harms, and since harms outside that set (e.g., non-English prompts) are invisible to any in-benchmark attacker, human evaluators remain indispensable.
